source.title: CLEAR: Revealing How Noise and Ambiguity Degrade Reliability in LLMs for Medicine
source.authors: Kevin H. Guo; Chao Yan; Avinash Baidya; Katherine E. Brown; Xiang Gao; Ju-Ming Xiong; Zhi-Jun Yin; B. Malin

record.tranche_reason: It measures downstream medical-question accuracy across model complexity, a different measure and setting from pretraining-loss scaling laws.
record.gate_note: The study reports medical QA accuracy and abstention results across model sizes. It does not measure held-out cross-entropy loss, training tokens or compute, fit power laws, or test compute-optimal allocations. Cited results from other studies are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates 17 off-the-shelf instruction-tuned models (1B–72B plus two GPT models) on perturbed medical QA. It reports how downstream accuracy, distractor robustness and abstention change with model size within families, which bears on V6 in a new setting. It fits no law and does not measure loss, so T3 fits better than T2.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors say larger models predictably gain closed-world accuracy and distractor resilience. Abstention shows no matching gain and sometimes a penalty, so the humility deficit widens with scale. They call this an inversion of scaling laws and say scaling alone does not fix reliability. They also note the distractor resilience gain is context-dependent and smaller on JAMA-CC.
record.recipe_differences: The study perturbs medical question-answer benchmarks and measures accuracy and abstention across instruction-tuned models; it does not measure pretraining loss or fit scaling laws.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary with benchmark and distractor count; the reported Qwen 2.5 penalty reduction from scaling is smaller on JAMA-CC than on MedQA.
record.code_released: The code for CLEAR will be released upon publication.
record.problems: For scaling-related results, most per-model values are presented in figures or supplementary figures rather than in the text; the text gives qualitative trends and a few penalty values. The study does not fit or validate a predictive scaling curve.
record.rows_left_out: Detailed per-model accuracy and abstention figures, including the broader model-by-dataset results in Figs. 2–5 and Supplementary Figs. S2–S8, were not extracted where the text did not state the result separately in words or provide a value. CoT comparisons were also left out because they do not report a model-size scaling result.

untested.parts: Prediction of downstream performance from pretraining loss; any fitted or extrapolated scaling curve; tasks outside medical multiple-choice QA; controlled scaling with fixed data and recipe.

record.verdict_notes: Scale comparisons use off-the-shelf instruction-tuned models, so size is confounded with training recipe. GPT model sizes are unknown, so the GPT-5.2 'highest accuracy, lowest abstention' point is not a size comparison. Most per-model values are only in figures not present in the text. The V6 verdicts rest on the authors' qualitative statements plus a few penalty numbers.

relationships.condition: Closed-world accuracy on MedQA/MedMCQA, within families (e.g. Qwen 2.5 1.5B→72B)
relationships.reason: Accuracy rises with model size (r1), and the per-distractor penalty halves from 1.5B to 72B on MedQA (r3 vs r2, r5 vs r4).
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy increased with model size, and the MedQA penalty per distractor halved between 1.5B and 72B.

relationships.reason: Scaling Qwen 2.5 to 72B cuts the penalty only 27% (r7 vs r6) and only 7.4%→7.1% for 2→3 distractors (from text, unrowed).
relationships.display_finding: Scaling Qwen 2.5 to 72B reduced the distractor penalty by only 27%, with penalties of 7.4% and 7.1% for two and three distractors.

relationships.condition: Open-world abstention tasks (truth replaced by NA/IDK/INA)
relationships.reason: Abstention does not improve in proportion to scale and the accuracy-abstention gap widens in Gemma 3 and Llama 3.x (r8, r9). The text also says larger models admit uncertainty least and scaling Qwen 2.5 does not help across framings.
relationships.display_finding: The accuracy–abstention gap widened in Gemma 3 and Llama 3.x, while larger models admitted uncertainty least and Qwen 2.5 scaling failed to help across framings.
